newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: NSW DOCTORS CONSIDER INDEFINITE STRIKE
Doctors look set to turn up the heat on the Federal Government over plans to restrict the number of GPs.

The Public Service Association, which represents three thousand hospital doctors in New South Wales, is to recommend indefinite strike action when doctors meet on February the 11th. The recommendation is in retaliation to plans by the Government to cap Medicare provider numbers for young doctors.
Doctors say a compromise reached with the Democrats is still unacceptable.

They say the agreement will mean those doctors who miss out on GP training courses will have to work in rural areas or stay in hospitals, a kind of forced labour they claim may contravene the constitution.
AUSTRALIA/FRANCE TIES TO BE STRENGTHENED
Ties between Australia and France are set to be considated in the wake of the nuclear testing row, with the re-instatement of an Australian defence attache in Paris.
Defence Minister Ian McLaughlan has met his French counterpart in Paris and was keen to stress that Canberra has put the nuclear testing issue behind it.
The position will be filled in the new year after being vacated in protest when French nuclear tests began last year.
TAX PACKAGE UNDER SCRUTINY FROM SMALL BUSINESS
The Federal Government's one-billion Family Tax Package has come under scrutiny following Opposition claims employment declarations will have to be continually adjusted under the scheme.
The initiative will either raise the tax-free threshold for families, or provide fortnightly payments depending on the age and number of children and total household income.
Chairman of the Council of Small Business Organisation, Ian Baldock, says if the package means household details will have to be constantly updated, there could be real problems.
Mr Baldock says the costs will be enormous especially in paperwork terms for workers, and in processing terms for employers.
CAMPBELL AIMS HIGH, DESPITE EARLY DISAPPOINTMENT
The West Australian election for the first time, saw the appearance of Graeme Campbell's Australia First Party.
The former Labor maverick put a brave face on what was an average result in the one lower house seat where his party fielded a candidate.
The Australia First candidate in the south west seat of Murray/Wellington received nine percent of the vote, which if extrapolated to a federal election would not be enough to win Senate seats.
Mr Campbell says the state poll took him by surprise but he will be much more organised by the next federal election.
He says his party will field a full Senate team in every state in the next federal election.
SNOWY MOUNTAINS SEARCH FOR TOURIST
A search is underway in the Snowy Mountains for a missing Dutch tourist.
Police say Jerome Doomernik, aged in his mid 20's planned to kayak two-kilometres down the Thredbo River.
He left Ngarigo Camping area at 6.30 last night, when he failed to arrive at his destination half an hour later, police were notified.
A search last night failed to find any trace of the tourist ... it's resuming again this morning.
STICKERS ON POKIES COULD WARN DANGERS OF GAMBLING

A local Council in Melbourne's north is considering placing stickers, warning of the dangers of gambling, on poker machines. The proposal is one of many being looked at by Banyule Council in developing its local gaming policy.
Under the policy, the Council will ask gaming machine applicants to provide clear evidence of the likely impact of gambling in a proposed area.
The Council says it wants to protect people who can't afford to gamble, from the impact of the machines.
